author: Emily Halling, Fox 21 News
title: Cloquet Area Fire District introduces telehealth technology in numerous ambulances | Health | fox21online.com
text:
CLOQUET, Minn. (KQDS-TV)- The rapid advancement in technology continues to develop before our eyes.
And while some technologies, including A.I. have raised alarms, other forms of it are assisting first responders.
The Cloquet Area Fire District is beginning a new era of responding to emergencies in their 200-mile radius, by introducing a new communication tool in several ambulances.
"We're doing a lot of work that the ER does, but out in the community with limited resources, so establishing this system is going to be another tool in the toolbox for our EMS providers," said Corey Larson, Assistant Fire Chief, Cloquet Area Fire District.
That tech is a brand-new telehealth system with a screen and microphones to connect with medical professionals before arriving to the emergency room.
AFC Corey Larson says that it speeds up the triage process.
"We're going to be able to get a hold of a doctor or healthcare provider as far as getting orders within a minute or two, and then another huge benefit is that that healthcare provider can actually see the patient, and we can interact in real time," explained AFC Corey Larson.
Cloquet Area Fire District is partnering with Avel eCare, the caretakers behind the screens. They have been operating nationwide for four years now, and have seen the success with this helpful tool.
"We have stories all the way from an EMT who was on their first call, and they looked up at the camera and said, "I remember talking about this in school. What should I take into the patient's house?" said John Gruber, EMS Operations Manager, Avel eCare.
The equipment will be installed in 3 out of the 4 ambulances in Cloquet..
And after some training, the first tele-health system in the region has gone live. Everyone involved, to help save lives in a brand-new way.
